data.cultural_impact: The name "Raghab" carries a rich cultural heritage, as it symbolizes a deep devotion and dedication towards Lord Rama. In Hinduism, Lord Rama is one of the avatars of the supreme god Vishnu, who is revered for his Supreme virtues- Dharma, Ardha, Neeta, and Shoka-shanti (righteousness, grace, knowledge, and peace). The name "Raghab" is a reminder of the pious actions, leadership qualities, and unwavering devotion of Lord Rama towards his people, which continues to inspire and influence Hindus even today. For instance, in the epic Ramayana, Raghubir (another name for Rama) embarks on a 14-year exile, renounces his kingdom, and bravely battles and defeats the enemy Ravana, who had abducted his wife Sita. As aresult, "Raghab" is an aspirational name for people who are committed to leading a life rooted in righteousness, morality, and compassion.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Raghib' also holds deep spiritual significance, as it evokes the feelings of an unwavering and surrendered devotion to Lord Rama. In Hinduism, God is viewed as the source of all existence, and devotion to the divine is considered an essential aspect of a pious and fulfilling life. The name 'Raghib' symbolizes the purity of a devotee's heart, who seeks refuge in Lord Rama during their spiritual journey. It is a call to surrender one's ego, desires, and attachments to the Almighty and develop a strong, steadfast, and unyielding connection with the divine. Moreover, the name 'Raghib' serves as a daily reminder of the ultimate goal of human life - attaining moksha or salvation, which comes only through the grace of God. Thus, the name 'Raghib' is a powerful tool for spiritual growth and transformation, encouraging individuals to lead a life marked by devotion, selflessness, and courage.

historical_references.reference: Raghab was a famous king of Kamarupa (Assam), who ruled from 1540 to 1560. He is also known as Raghab Singha. His reign marked the end of the medieval period in Assam and the beginning of the early modern period. Raghab Singha expanded his territory, founded new towns, and implemented various social and religious reforms.
historical_references.context: Medieval to Early Modern period in Assam

historical_references.reference: Another Raghab, known as Raghavan, was a revered saint and philosopher in South India. He is believed to have lived between the 13th and 15th centuries. Raghavan was a prominent figure in the Bhakti movement, which emphasized devotion to God through love and emotion. He is known for his works in Tamil literature, including the 'Ramayana' commentary 'Guru-Govinda-Doha-Samasya' and the 'Aksharaman Malai', which is a collection of hymns.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Raghab is of Hindu origin and means having the capacity to give great joy. In the modern context, this name has been associated with various trends. One such trend is devotional music, where Raghab is a popular name for a genre of music that is deeply rooted in Hinduism. Another trend is spiritualism, where Raghab is seen as a symbol of compassion and love, often used in meditation and mindfulness practices. Lastly, Raghab is also a trending name in self-help and personal growth, where it is associated with the idea of having the capacity to bring joy and positivity into one's own life and the lives of others.
